known_research_boundaries: Reconstruct a seasonal cycle at Meybod around1900. This date is an editorial anchor within the documented long use of the type, not a claim to a preserved daybook. The architecture and functions are drawn from field research and engineering papers. Key contradiction resolved: later papers loosely call these ancient refrigerators, while Jørgensen explicitly distinguishes ice storage from food refrigeration. Say ice cooled drinks and could be used elsewhere; do not put hanging food inside the store. Avoid400BCE origin claims, exact historical freezing yields, fixed melt percentages, huge radiant-cold arrows, mechanical windcatchers, and a claim that a small dome vent creates the freezing. Engineering models are explanatory, not measurements from1900; their own reported yields vary with assumptions. Some METU wording says transfer on hot summer days in its wall section; do not use that to move winter harvesting into summer. Water, operating labor and maintenance are central to the story. Final costume follows late-Qajar ordinary layered clothing, not court finery.
